title: Texas Camp Hit by Floods Must Be Under Trustee, Families Say
summary: Camp Mystic, the Texas girls camp where 28 people were killed in flash floods last summer, should be taken over by a bankruptcy trustee who can settle lawsuits filed against the company and the family blamed for the deaths, a committee of parents said in a court filing.

title: Yuan Steps Into Carry Trade Spotlight Over Yen, Analysts Say
summary: The Chinese yuan is gaining renewed attention as a currency to fund carry trades as a surging yen forces investors to seek alternatives, strategists say.

title: Asian Chip Stocks Rise, Crude Climbs Toward $100: Markets Wrap
summary: Asian chip stocks extended their recent gains on sustained investor interest in the artificial-intelligence trade. Escalating hostilities in the Middle East pushed Brent crude toward $100 a barrel.

title: Ringgit Falls to Lowest Versus Singapore Dollar Since November
summary: Malaysia’s ringgit fell to a 10-month low versus the Singapore dollar, weighed by foreign stock outflows while the island state’s currency is supported by a hawkish monetary policy stance.

title: Ex-US Trade Representative: US-Canada Ties Remain Vital
summary: Former US Trade Representative Susan Schwab says shared geography and deep economic ties will keep the U.S. and Canada aligned despite upcoming political friction. She notes that joint cooperation on critical minerals and a unified front against Chinese competition are essential to protect North American industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NSE Cuts IPO Price Range, Giving Up Shot at India’s Top Listing
summary: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. has lowered the price range for its long-awaited initial public offering and may shrink the stake on sale, according to people familiar with the matter, putting what was set to be India’s biggest-ever listing out of reach.

title: Mexico Slashes Pemex Aid by 70% to $4.8 Billion in New Budget
summary: Mexico’s government aims to reduce its financial support for state-owned oil company Petroleos Mexicanos’ debt payments to 81.1 billion pesos ($4.8 billion) in 2027, down by nearly 70% from the 263.5 billion pesos budgeted this year.

title: BOK's Rhee: FX Intervention Can Calm Volatility
summary: Rhee Chang Yong says he was surprised that the recent market intervention appeared to be mainly by Japan and the US rather than a broader G7 effort that would typically include European countries. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Plans to Let $568 Billion Fund Tap Southbound Bond Connect
summary: China plans to allow its $568 billion social security fund to buy offshore bonds through an investment channel with Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter, in its latest effort to boost demand for yuan assets in the Asian financial hub.

title: Hedge Funds Bet Yen Will Strengthen Beyond 150 by Year-End
summary: Hedge funds are betting dollar-yen will fall below 150 by year-end with some longer-dated options trades targeting a move as low as 140.

title: India Shuns Pomp In Favor Of Restraint at Subdued BRICS Summit
summary: Three years ago, New Delhi put on a spectacle when world leaders descended on India’s capital for the Group of 20 summit. Colorful murals of Indian mythology adorned the city alongside elaborate statues, floral arrangements and welcome billboards featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 9
summary: Brent oil moved closer to $100 a barrel after the US struck Iranian tankers near the vital crude-export hub of Kharg Island, stoking fears of deeper disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Bessent Dares Traders on Yen Bets: ‘I Am the House Now’
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged traders to counter his efforts to strengthen Japan’s currency, touting that when he makes market calls nowadays he’s effectively doing so with inside information. Bloomberg's Sunny Bangia breaks down the news. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasury Buybacks Won't Fix US Yields, Strategist Says
summary: Lombard Odier Senior Macro Strategist Homin Lee argues that expanded Treasury buybacks won't solve underlying US yield pressures driven by large deficits. While the plan may offer short-term relief, he emphasizes that broader macroeconomic factors will continue to dictate yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: A Sports Mogul's Empire Under Scrutiny
summary: Mark Walter pioneered how insurance companies invest policyholders' payments. His dealmaking spawned an empire that included some of the world's most famous sports franchises. But now, that empire is under scrutiny. (Corrects title of video at 1:38.) (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Holds Decline as Mideast Tensions Bolster Rate-Hike Case
summary: Gold held a three-day decline, as fresh attacks on ships in the Middle East added to inflationary risks and raised prospects for a US interest-rate hike.

title: China’s AI-Fueled IPO Boom Delivers Six-figure Windfalls to Retail Investors
summary: Six months’ salary in a single day. That’s the kind of payoff China’s boom in initial public offerings is handing to a lucky few.

title: China Banks Snap Up Bonds to Seek Returns as Loan Slump Deepens
summary: Chinese banks are increasingly buying government bonds to improve returns as a depressed mortgage and consumer loan market leaves them with few options to deploy capital.

title: Bessent’s ‘Fever’-Cooling Debt Buybacks Put Wall St. on Edge
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to reveal how far he’s initially willing to go restrain US bond yields via an expanded buyback program that has Wall Street dealers on edge.

title: El Niño Causes Panama Canal to Restrict Traffic
summary: Ilya Espino de Marotta is the new head of the Panama Canal Authority and she is already tackling some tough challenges. She says a strong El Niño has led to restrictions on ship transits and talks about how this weather pattern is impacting the business. She speaks to Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: A Case Against the "Conventional Wisdom" of Investing
summary: In his new book 'The Awesome Portfolio', Jared Dillian makes the argument against the conventional wisdom to invest your cash as "you buy the index, you dollar cost average, you hold, you ride out the volatility." He argues "cash can also be your friend." He joins Businessweek Daily to discuss he new book and latest market headlines. (Source: Bloomberg)
